name: rfc7541-hpack-table-capacity
description: Audit HPACK dynamic-table capacity negotiation and size-update timing per RFC 7541 §4.2/§6.3 — encoder-chosen values above the SETTINGS limit must be decoding errors, size updates must appear at the start of the first header block after a change, and multiple changes must signal the smallest value (at most two updates); divergent interpretations become COMPRESSION_ERROR interoperability bombs and table-eviction holes (related nghttp2/nghttp2#1660 interpretation-divergence empirical finding; Google Cloud ALB temporarily degraded dynamic tables to mitigate a client bug; apache.hc.core5 5.3.1 fi…

name: rfc7636
description: RFC 7636: Proof Key for Code Exchange by OAuth Public Clients. Defines PKCE extension for OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow, mitigating authorization code interception attacks by introducing code_verifier and code_challenge parameters. Enables secure OAuth usage for public clients like mobile apps and SPAs.

name: rfc8176
description: RFC 8176 - Authentication Method Reference Values. Establishes IANA registry for amr claim values in JWT tokens, defining standard identifiers for authentication methods including biometrics (face, fingerprint, iris, retina, voice), password, OTP, MFA, smart card, SMS, and more. Use when working with JWT amr claims, authentication method identifiers, or OpenID Connect authentication context.

name: rfc9000-ack-range-validation
description: Audit whether QUIC implementations validate ACK-frame acknowledgment ranges per RFC 9000 §13.1/§21.4 — acknowledging unsent packets, malformed ACK ranges, or undetected optimistic ACKs become a congestion-control-deception DDoS-amplification primitive (related CVE-2025-4820/CVE-2025-4821 quiche < 0.24.4; ANRW 2025: 11 of 16 Interop implementations vulnerable)

name: rfc9000-close-draining-state
description: Audit QUIC implementations' frame-handling obligations during the closing/draining states per RFC 9000 §10.2 — the closing state may only retransmit CONNECTION_CLOSE; the draining state MUST send nothing and process nothing; violations open the connection-close state machine as an attack surface (related CVE-2024-45396 Quicly draining-state ACK handling assertion failure, QUIC-FUZZ empirical; xquic Stateless Reset / VN log NULL dereference; nginx QUIC CVE-2024-31079/32760/34161/35200 single-session worker-crash family)

name: rfc9000-connection-id-retirement
description: Audit QUIC implementations' handling of Connection ID lifecycle obligations (NEW_CONNECTION_ID / RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID / active_connection_id_limit) for symmetry — asymmetric obligations create a memory-exhaustion attack surface (related CVE-2024-22189, 7.5 HIGH)

name: rfc9000-flow-control-accounting
description: Audit QUIC implementations' stream-level/connection-level flow-control accounting and limit enforcement per RFC 9000 §4 — accounting errors open memory-exhaustion or integer-wraparound attack surfaces (related CVE-2024-22189, CVE-2023-49295)

name: rfc9000-handshake-done-timing
description: Audit QUIC server handling of HANDSHAKE_DONE frame send-timing and receipt processing per RFC 9000 §19.20 and RFC 9001 §4.9.2 — timing and key-discard-order errors can be triggered by a malicious server/peer into assertion crashes (related CVE-2025-59530 quic-go, observed in the wild)

name: rfc9000-migration-congestion-window
description: Audit whether QUIC implementations violate the RFC 9000 §8.1 anti-amplification 3x limit and §9.4 pre-validation rate-limiting obligations during connection migration / NAT rebinding — sending at full speed to an unvalidated address opens a UDP reflection-amplification and traffic-hijacking attack surface (related CVE-2026-35191 OpenSSL QUIC non-validating-mode accounting error violating 3x; TMA 2025: 20% of IPv4 servers violate the amplification limit; HAProxy#3329 disable_active_migration over-interpretation empirical finding)

name: rfc9000-new-token-replay
description: Audit QUIC implementations' protection of NEW_TOKEN frames and cross-connection token replay per RFC 9000 §19.7/§8.1.4 — single-use constraints, the IP-binding MUST, and unlimited replay would let the address-validation system be bypassed (blind-spot clause; format custom + scattered MUSTs = high-variance surface)

name: rfc9000-path-validation-amplification
description: Audit QUIC implementations' enforcement of path validation and anti-amplification limits per RFC 9000 §8.1/§8.2.1/§9 — missing PATH_CHALLENGE/PATH_RESPONSE obligations or unenforced anti-amplification limits become an unauthenticated DoS amplification primitive (related CVE-2023-49295 quic-go, HIGH)

name: rfc9000-stateless-reset-token
description: Audit QUIC implementations' stateless-reset-token generation, secrecy, and collision handling per RFC 9000 §10.3/§21.11 — derivable / leaked / reused tokens let connections be killed remotely, and the Stateless Reset Oracle configuration surface is an amplifier (related CVE-2026-50009 Netty < 4.2.15.Final; xquic/Quicly fuzz empirical findings)

name: rfc9000-stream-reset-cancel
description: Audit whether QUIC stream reset/cancel (RESET_STREAM/STOP_SENDING) state-machine validation and cost symmetry comply with RFC 9000 §3.4/§3.5 — Final Size invariants, missing STREAM_STATE_ERROR on state mismatch, and cancellation cost far below server processing cost (H3 Rapid Reset DoS surface; related CVE-2023-44487 same-pattern in HTTP/2, H3 stacks advised to mitigate proactively; 2025 MadeYouReset variant proves the family keeps evolving)

name: rfc9000-transport-parameter-validation
description: Audit whether QUIC implementations validate transport-parameter integrity and consistency per RFC 9000 §18.2/§7.3 — missing/mismatched CID-related parameters, client carrying server-only parameters, illegal values not rejected (pre-authentication attack surface and MITM CID-injection surface; blind-spot clause; CVE-2025-54939 lsquic QUIC-LEAK evidences the same path)

name: rfc9001-0rtt-replay-protection
description: Audit whether QUIC implementations enforce 0-RTT anti-replay protection per RFC 9001 §9.2 (MUST implement and use TLS 1.3 anti-replay) and §5.6 (application protocols MUST define a 0-RTT profile) — the same 0-RTT flight accepted twice by the same instance, or a non-idempotent request executed twice, is the replay attack surface (related quiche issue#2678 confirmed: 0-RTT exact-flight replay accepted twice, violating the RFC 8446 §8 at-most-once-per-instance MUST; anchor RFC 9114 §10.9 requires H3 to apply RFC 8470 anti-replay)

name: rfc9001-retry-integrity-tag
description: Audit whether QUIC implementations handle Retry-packet integrity and token lifecycle per RFC 9000 §8.1.4/§17.2.5 and RFC 9001 §5.8 — unverified integrity tag, replayable tokens, unguarded multi-Retry loops (pre-authentication attack surface; blind-spot clause; warpsock added §17.2.5.1/§17.2.5.2 loop guards as evidence)

name: rfc9113-content-length-data-mismatch
description: Audit HTTP/2 implementations' consistency check between Content-Length and the sum of DATA frame lengths — in H2 Content-Length has no transfer meaning, but when forwarded/downgraded verbatim into H1 it regains semantics and becomes request smuggling (related CVE-2021-21295 Netty <4.1.60 H2→H1 downgrade smuggling and the 4.1.61 follow-up fix; CVE-2026-58055 nghttpx ≤1.69.0 Upgrade+CL keep-alive smuggling; sibling/complementary to the H3-side rfc9114-content-length-data-mismatch)

name: rfc9113-continuation-header-limit
description: Audit HTTP/2 implementations' enforcement of CONTINUATION frames and header-block size limits — buffering unbounded oversized header blocks just to return a 413, or END_HEADERS never set, leads to memory-exhaustion DoS (related CVE-2024-27316 Apache httpd 2.4.17-2.4.58 nghttp2 buffering memory exhaustion; CERT VU#421644 frame-class disclosure; CVE-2024-24549 Tomcat and CVE-2024-30255 Envoy sibling variants)

name: rfc9113-flow-control-window-stall
description: Audit the symmetry and boundedness of HTTP/2 flow-control-window (WINDOW_UPDATE) implementations — window manipulation forcing the server to queue data at 1-byte granularity is Data Dribble (CVE-2019-9511, CVSS 7.5); zero-increment WINDOW_UPDATE is an illegal frame, and a server that answers each with RST_STREAM enables the MadeYouReset resource-consumption chain (CVE-2025-5115 Jetty GHSA-mmxm-8w33-wc4h); INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE=0 plus trickle WINDOW_UPDATE Slowloris holds form the hold half of the HTTP/2 Bomb (CVE-2026-49975/47774); RFC 9113 §5.2/§6.9 define window semantics but the "stalled-str…

name: rfc9113-goaway-drain-lifecycle
description: Audit the HTTP/2 connection-termination lifecycle (GOAWAY draining and RST_STREAM races) — concurrent RST_STREAM and GOAWAY triggering a write-pipeline race can permanently block worker threads until the thread pool is exhausted (CVE-2026-12611 Jetty GHSA-gpg9-4257-cfm3: HTTP2Flusher.terminated reset to null by the race, queued items never processed); nginx graceful shutdown leaking GOAWAY on H2 connections causes worker hangs (2024-05 kaseiwang patch + http2-grace-shutdown-test PoC); RFC 9113 §6.8 defines the double-GOAWAY graceful-shutdown sequence, but the race window and termination one-w…

name: rfc9113-h2c-upgrade-pseudoheader
description: Audit h2c upgrade negotiation and pseudo-header validation — a reverse proxy forwarding Upgrade: h2c + HTTP2-Settings opens a raw-byte tunnel that bypasses authentication/WAF (CVE-2026-88008 Traefik GHSA-w4v4-9rw7-5326 CVSS 9.1 CWE-444+863, fixed in PR #13797 stripping the h2c token; CVE-2026-88011 v2 sibling; CVE-2026-73548 Envoy generic-upgrade smuggling); HTTP2-Settings must not be forwarded with requests (RFC 9113 §3.2), and pseudo-header rules (§8.3) are the audit anchors; BishopFox h2csmuggler demonstrated default forwarding in HAProxy/Traefik/Nuster as early as 2020

name: rfc9113-ping-empty-frame-flood
description: Audit whether HTTP/2 implementations bound the processing cost of mandatory-response frames (PING) and empty frames (DATA/HEADERS/CONTINUATION/PUSH_PROMISE) — PING forces a per-frame ACK (CVE-2019-9512 Ping Flood: sustained PING inflates the response queue, exhausting CPU/memory); empty frames bypass flow control with asymmetric per-frame cost (CVE-2019-9518 Empty Frame Flood, disclosed with Envoy security-team acknowledgment); zero-length header memory residency (CVE-2019-9516 Header Leak); RFC 9113 §6.7/§6.1 give the semantics but no cost guardrails

name: rfc9113-priority-tree-abuse
description: Audit whether HTTP/2 priority-tree implementations resist resource exhaustion via cycles — continuously reshuffling priorities across many streams churns the tree structure and exhausts CPU (CVE-2019-9513 Resource Loop: nghttp2/nginx/netty/undertow full-stack impact, CVSS 7.5, fixed in nghttp2 1.39.2); RFC 9113 §5.3 permits implementations to deprioritize processing (blank-clause escape), but "if you keep it, it must resist churn" — the audit target is the boundedness of the priority state machine

name: rfc9113-rapid-reset-concurrency
description: Audit HTTP/2 implementations' concurrency-limit accounting and forced-close obligations per RFC 9113 §5.1.2/§6.4 — only open/half-closed streams count toward concurrency (closed releases the slot immediately), RST_STREAM closes without acknowledgment so "open then cancel" consumes no concurrency slot; without a connection-level work budget this is the original CVE-2023-44487 Rapid Reset vulnerability surface (Google/AWS/Cloudflare all affected, one of the largest L7 DDoS events in history, 2023-10; variants: batched delayed cancel, over-limit stream opens relying on per-stream rejection)

name: rfc9113-server-push-lifecycle
description: Audit HTTP/2 server-push (PUSH_PROMISE / reserved-stream) lifecycle implementations — enabling push is an attack-surface amplifier: Cache-Digest header triggering a crash on push (CVE-2020-9490 Apache httpd 2.4.20-2.4.43, CVSS 7.5, mitigated by H2Push off); push-method access-control failure (CVE-2023-30631 Apache Traffic Server push_method_enabled config ineffective, CVSS 7.5); http4s Ember push-frame DoS (CVE-2026-69203, mitigated by proxy stripping PUSH_PROMISE); RFC 9113 §6.6/§8.4 require that clients can reject push and servers can advertise ENABLE_PUSH=0, but reserved-stream state-machi…

name: rfc9113-settings-frame-flood
description: Audit whether HTTP/2 implementations bound SETTINGS-frame processing — repeatedly sending SETTINGS frames with an excessive entry count exhausts CPU (CVE-2020-11080 nghttp2 <1.41.0: a 14,400-byte frame with 2,400 entries repeated saturates the CPU, impacting the entire ecosystem including Node.js/Oracle MySQL); the RFC only requires the length-multiple-of-6 check and in-order processing — an entry-count cap is the implementation's obligation (blind-spot clause)

name: rfc9113-stream-state-machine
description: Audit HTTP/2 stream-state-machine handling of illegal frame transitions — DATA on a half-closed(remote) stream and similar violations must be answered with STREAM_CLOSED, and manufacturing them in bulk becomes the MadeYouReset resource drain (CVE-2025-5115 Jetty GHSA-mmxm-8w33-wc4h); the HEADERS+RST_STREAM race with double callbacks and double cleanup can cause double-free (Apache h2_mplx.c, disclosed 2026); the RST_STREAM refused-stream path forcing an in-scope write can cause heap UAF (CVE-2026-56848 Node.js, fixed in commit ba6cb5c); sustained RST floods leaking memory on connection close…

name: rfc9114-content-length-data-mismatch
description: Audit whether HTTP/3 targets violate RFC 9114 §4.1.2 — the Content-Length value must equal the sum of received DATA frame lengths; a violation that gets forwarded implies an H3→H1 request-smuggling surface (related CVE-2026-33555 HAProxy)

name: rfc9114-goaway-drain-enforcement
description: Audit whether HTTP/3 implementations enforce GOAWAY graceful-shutdown semantics strictly per RFC 9114 §5.2/§7.2.6 — identifier monotonicity, rejecting new requests after receipt, and the conservative default on GOAWAY-less shutdown (evidence: quiche#2700, quic-go#5326, erlang_quic 1.0.0 fix; no standalone CVE)

name: rfc9114-grease-reserved-frames
description: Audit whether HTTP/3 implementations meet the tolerance obligations for GREASE/reserved frame types, reserved SETTINGS identifiers, and unknown unidirectional stream types per RFC 9114 §9/§7.2.8 — unknown frames must be length-skipped, never rejected; H2 reserved frames 0x02/0x06/0x08/0x09 must kill the connection, never be GREASE-skipped; rejecting GREASE is a forward-compatibility break (evidence: aioquic <1.6 stream-tail GREASE frame caused stream-data loss; confusing reserved frames with H2 smuggling frames opens a smuggling backdoor)

name: rfc9114-pseudo-header-field-validation
description: Audit whether HTTP/3 targets handle malformed pseudo-headers/fields strictly per RFC 9114 §4.1.2/§4.2/§4.3 malformed judgments — lenient handling implies a parsing-split and H3→H1 smuggling attack surface (related nginx#1043 unfixed; H2 historical pattern replicated)

name: rfc9114-qpack-decoded-size-limit
description: Audit whether HTTP/3 targets limit only the compressed QPACK frame length but not the decoded field-section size — no decoded-size limit means a compression-amplification memory-exhaustion attack surface (thousands-fold amplification per connection possible; related CVE-2025-64702/CVE-2026-40898 quic-go, CVE-2026-12523 quiche, CVE-2025-13945 Wireshark)

name: rfc9114-server-push-frame-rejection
description: Audit whether HTTP/3 clients/servers strictly reject server-push legacy frames — PUSH_PROMISE and MAX_PUSH_ID receipt must terminate the connection with H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED (RFC 9114 §7.2.5/§7.2.7); silently swallowing them means a missing protocol-error obligation (evidence: quic-go#5686, inconsistent handling within the same function in v0.60.0)

name: rfc9114-settings-frame-order
description: Audit whether HTTP/3 implementations enforce SETTINGS-frame strictness per RFC 9114 §7.2.1 — SETTINGS must be the first frame on each control stream, and a duplicate SETTINGS must be treated as an H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED connection error (blind-spot clause, no public CVE yet)

name: rfc9114-trailers-frame-sequence
description: Audit whether HTTP/3 implementations handle trailer and multi-HEADERS frame sequences per RFC 9114 §4.1/§4.2 — DATA after trailing HEADERS is a connection error, trailer vs Content-Length consistency, missing validation of duplicate response header sections is an H3-layer message-smuggling surface (blind-spot clause; nginx#1043 same ecosystem; H2 trailer/CL historical smuggling pattern replicated)

name: rfc9204-qpack-dynamic-table-capacity
description: Audit whether QPACK dynamic-table capacity negotiation and size-update ordering strictly follow RFC 9204 §3.2 — over-capacity insertion and out-of-order size updates are encoder/decoder stream errors, a compression-layer state-machine attack surface of the same family as CVE-2025-64702

name: rfc9218-priority-update-validation
description: Audit whether HTTP/3 implementations' validation of the PRIORITY_UPDATE frame (RFC 9218 §7.2) is complete — frame position, target stream type, out-of-limit stream IDs, push-stream references, and priority field-value parse failures are all connection-error obligations whose absence is a blind-spot clause (erlang_quic Strict PRIORITY_UPDATE parsing fix as evidence)

name: rfc9297-capsule-content-length
description: Audit whether HTTP Datagrams / Capsule Protocol implementations strictly follow RFC 9297 §3.2/§3.3/§3.5 — capsule coexisting with Content-Length and other headers, truncated capsules, and unknown capsule-type handling errors are an HTTP-smuggling same-family attack surface (same family: an undisclosed sharing-session smuggling case, CVE-2025-64702 pattern)

name: rfc9368-version-negotiation-validation
description: Audit whether QUIC implementations handle version negotiation and downgrade protection per RFC 8999 §6 and RFC 9368 §4 — Version Negotiation packet invariants and the full set of Version Information validation MUSTs; their absence is a version-downgrade and parse-crash attack surface (evidence: QUIC-FUZZ xquic VN-event crash; CVE-2024-45396 Quicly same-family pattern)

name: rfc9457-problem-details
description: Design and implement HTTP API error responses using RFC 9457 "Problem Details" (application/problem+json, application/problem+xml). Use when building or reviewing REST/HTTP API error handling, defining error response formats, creating custom problem types, or migrating from RFC 7807. Covers the standard members (type, status, title, detail, instance), extension members, multiple-error reporting, and security considerations.

name: rfc9457-problem-details
description: Design and review HTTP API error responses using RFC 9457 Problem Details (application/problem+json, application/problem+xml). Use when implementing API error handling, defining new problem types, validating error response payloads, or migrating from RFC 7807.

name: rfc9700
description: RFC 9700: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security (BCP 240). Updates RFCs 6749, 6750, and 6819 with security requirements for OAuth clients, authorization servers, and resource servers. Use when implementing or reviewing OAuth or OpenID Connect flows, PKCE and downgrade prevention, redirect URI validation, CSRF and mix-up defenses, access token restrictions, refresh token rotation, or migration away from implicit and password grants.

name: rfc_adherence_audit

Invoke when creating a new RFC adherence record, refreshing an existing one after code changes, or filling in the catalog for an RFC that has no record yet.

description: Use when you need to demonstrate that a mapping-derived signal (e.g. a shift, bias, or clustering pattern) is algorithm-independent by repeating the same alignment on identical input FASTQ with multiple aligners and comparing downstream distributions.

name: rna-seq-read-alignment-star
description: Use when preprocessing labeled SPLiT-seq FASTQ reads (e.g., SCSit output with combinatorial barcodes and UMI) need to be aligned to mm10, hg19, or a combined mm10-hg19 reference to compare mapped-read yields.

name: rna-seq-read-count-aggregation-per-node
description: Use when a KEGG pathway node contains multiple functionally homologous genes (e.g., the 4-gene ALDH3A1 node in hsa00340 or the 21-gene PLA2G4B node in hsa00564) and you need one node-level read count and regulation value instead of per-gene ambiguity.

name: rna-seq-read-depth-subsampling
description: Use when benchmarking fusion-gene detection sensitivity (or similar read-count-dependent callers) across decreasing sequencing depths from a single deeply sequenced paired-end FASTQ sample.

name: rna-seq-read-fragmentation
description: Use when training or fairly benchmarking fixed-length read classifiers (e.g., viRNAtrap vs DeepVirFinder, DeepViFi, ViraMiner, Seq2Seq) and you need viral and human transcripts converted into comparable 48 bp fragments with shared train/test splits.

name: rna-seq-read-mapping-parameter-tuning
description: Use when when comparing two implementations of the same RNA-seq mapping algorithm on identical reference indices and read sets, if per-read mapping agreement is <99.8% or the overall mapping rate differs by >0.

name: rna-seq-read-pseudoalignment-quantification
description: Use when you need to quantify reads supporting annotated and novel splicing events from short-read RNA-seq FASTQ files faster than a spliced aligner (fortuna was ~7x faster and mapped reads with mismatches across novel junctions more accurately).

name: rna-seq-read-quantification
description: Use when raw FASTQ RNA-seq reads from a model or non-model eukaryote must be converted to a KO-level count table, especially when no reference transcriptome exists or when cross-version equivalence with Kallisto-based quantification must be checked.

name: rna-seq-read-realignment-to-masked-genome
description: Use when per-allele read counts at heterozygous biallelic SNPs show inflated reference allele ratios (e.g. ~51.8–51.9% instead of the expected 50%) and you suspect the reference genome biases alignment toward the reference allele.

name: rna-seq-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking junction/splicing-event detection accuracy on controlled data: you need simulated FASTQs with known held-out novel junctions and per-event-type recall/precision ground truth.

name: rna-seq-read-simulation-from-count-matrices
description: Use when you need simulated RNA-seq FASTQ data whose underlying expression counts contain a known, controlled differential expression pattern for teaching or validating DESeq2/Salmon workflows.

name: rna-seq-read-simulation-with-rsem
description: Use when a benchmark requires a ground-truth RNA-Seq dataset with known transcript provenance, so assembler completeness (95%-assembled genes/isoforms), accuracy (misassemblies), and duplication ratio can be evaluated against a reference transcriptome.

name: rna-seq-read-truncation-processing
description: Use when you need to generate derivative sequencing-length variants (single-end truncations of paired-end FASTQ reads) to test robustness of an expression quantification metric across sequencing lengths and strategies.

name: rna-seq-regulon-gene-list-processing
description: Use when two or more differentially expressed gene sets (e.g. H-NS and LuxR regulons from RNA-seq comparisons) must be intersected to count shared regulators/genes, with identifiers harmonized first.

name: rna-seq-replicate-reproducibility-analysis
description: Use when you have read counts or rank lists for the same transcript/gene set from two replicate RNA-seq experiments (within-lab or between-lab, e.g. SEQC comparisons) and need to quantify reproducibility with error control at a target mFDR such as alpha = 0.01.

name: rna-seq-sample-outlier-detection
description: Use when an RNA-Seq or expression dataset with sample metadata (condition, organ, tumor status) needs a QC pass to confirm that within-condition samples are consistent and to flag outlier samples before differential expression analysis.

name: rna-seq-sequencing-depth-quantification
description: Use when you need gene- and tissue-specific sequencing depth predictions (in millions of reads) for splice junction coverage of a gene panel, e.g. deciding which GTEx biosample and depth to use for RNA-seq mis-splicing surveillance.

name: rna-seq-shape-change-annotation
description: Use when SCISSOR has flagged shape-change outliers (e.g., ScissorOutput$GSC / $LSC sample IDs) and you need to determine which detected aberrations correspond to existing mutation calls versus novel events.

name: rna-seq-short-read-alignment
description: Use when aligning RNA-Seq FASTQ files inside a systemPipeR workflow and you need to choose or benchmark an aligner (Bowtie2/TopHat2 vs HISAT2/Rsubread) or verify near-linear parallel speedup via clusterRun.

name: rna-seq-short-read-alignment
description: Use when FASTQ RNA-Seq reads (single- or paired-end Illumina) must be spliced-aligned to a reference genome before expression estimation, and novel junction discovery should be suppressed in favor of known annotated junctions.

name: rna-seq-signature-count-augmentation
description: Use when an RNA-seq quantification based on fortuna signature counts (cnt.tsv/alt.tsv from --quant) must account for novel splice junctions that an aligner like STAR found in previously unmapped reads.

name: rna-seq-spanning-read-cluster-analysis
description: Use when RNA-Seq read support at a fusion locus forms multiple spanning-read junction clusters and one must decide which cluster is the primary fusion junction versus alternative-splice or backsplice junctions.

name: rna-seq-splice-event-quantification
description: Use when you need to detect and count novel alternative splicing events (ES, IR, AA, AD, AP, IE) from RNA-seq FASTQs using only a GTF annotation and genome FASTA, without a spliced aligner, or when tissue-specific event catalogs (e.g. RPM >= 1) are needed.

name: rna-seq-spliced-read-alignment

name: rna-seq-spliced-read-alignment

name: rna-seq-sra-read-acquisition

name: rna-seq-statistical-filtering

name: rna-seq-tmm-normalization-log2-cpm

name: rna-seq-tpm-expression-retrieval

name: rna-seq-tpm-integration

name: rna-seq-transcript-abundance-quantification
description: Use when starting from RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. Polyester-simulated paired-end reads) and transcript-level abundance estimates or a gene-level count matrix are needed for differential expression analysis.

name: rna-seq-transcript-assembly
description: Use when you have splice-aware BAM alignments of RNA-seq reads from one or more aligners (e.g., Hisat2 and Star) mapped to a reference genome and need to assemble transcripts, especially lowly expressed ones missed by single-aligner assemblers.

name: rna-seq-transcript-assembly
description: Use when raw RNA-Seq FASTQ samples (e.g., 180 TARGET osteosarcoma tumors plus 9 normal bone controls) must be converted into a consensus transcript candidate set prior to novel lncRNA detection.

name: rna-seq-transcript-quantification
description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files from GEO/ENA (disease and control samples) must be converted to per-sample isoform-level TPM abundances as input for isoform switching / dMDT calling in the CanIsoNet workflow.

name: rna-seq-transcriptome-assembly-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing de novo transcriptome assemblers across datasets with different gene-detection depths, especially when raw counts of assembled genes are unfair and a Kallisto-normalized fraction of 95%-assembled genes is needed for cross-dataset ranking.

name: rna-seq-treatment-response-classification
description: Use when classifying binary treatment response (e.g. rituximab responders vs non-responders in the R4RA E-MTAB-11611 cohort) from transcriptomic matrices where predictors vastly outnumber samples (P >> n) and an honest out-of-sample AUC is required.

name: rna-seq-workflow-environment-generation
description: Use when a user needs to rapidly test or run a complete pre-configured RNA-Seq NGS workflow in R/Bioconductor, from environment generation through execution to HTML scientific reporting.

name: rna-sequence-error-rate-quantification
description: Use when aligned ONT direct RNA reads (BAM) against an mRNA reference are available and you need a total error rate plus mismatch/deletion/insertion decomposition, or to compare dRNA-specific per-nucleotide error biases against matched plasmid/cDNA sequencing.

name: rna-sequence-feature-computation
description: Use when per-tool TP/FP/FN bin classifications from an m6A dRNA-seq benchmark need to be explained by sequence context (motif variant, GC, structure, entropy).

name: rna-sequence-feature-extraction

name: rna-sequence-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw RNA transcript sequences in FASTA format must be converted into the numeric feature set (SIFs, SS k-mer scores, ORF, protein features) that LncDC's XGBoost model consumes for lncRNA prediction, or when reproducing its SSF ablation experiments.

name: rna-sequence-identity-reduction
description: Use when building train/test splits of RNA fragments (e.g., 51-nt pseudouridine-site windows) where homologous sequences across folds would inflate prediction accuracy through leakage.

name: rna-sequence-one-hot-encoding

name: rna-sequence-one-hot-encoding
description: Use when raw RNA sequence segments (e.g., 41-nt tissue-specific m6A positive/negative samples) must be converted into fixed-length numeric feature matrices before feeding a CNN or other fixed-input neural network model.

name: rna-structural-content-figure-generation
description: Use when you have an RNA secondary structure in CT (connectivity table) or dot-bracket FASTA format plus a tab-delimited per-nucleotide Shannon entropy file, and you need BPC/entropy plots and structure-count heatmap/histogram outputs.

name: rna-structure-basepair-content-filtering

name: rna-structure-lineplot-visualization
description: Use when you have an RNA secondary structure (CT or dot-bracket format) plus a per-nucleotide Shannon entropy file and need per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed SE line plots (e.g. reproducing Supplementary Fig. S2A/B for HCV_Jc1).

name: rna-structure-ncrna-search
description: Searches for non-coding RNA homologs and classifies RNA families using Infernal covariance model searches against the Rfam database. Identifies structured RNAs by sequence and secondary structure conservation. Use when querying sequences against Rfam, building custom covariance models for novel RNA families, or classifying non-coding transcripts by family.

name: rna-structure-secondary-structure-prediction
description: Predicts RNA secondary structures using minimum free energy folding and partition function analysis with ViennaRNA (RNAfold, RNAalifold, RNAcofold). Computes base-pair probabilities, centroid structures, and consensus structures from alignments. Use when predicting RNA folding, evaluating structural stability, or comparing structures across homologs.

name: rna-structure-structure-probing
description: Analyzes experimental RNA structure probing data from SHAPE-MaP and DMS-MaPseq experiments using ShapeMapper2. Converts mutation rates to per-nucleotide reactivity profiles that constrain structure prediction. Use when processing SHAPE-MaP or DMS-MaPseq sequencing data to obtain experimental RNA structure information.

name: rna-transcript-dataset-construction

description: Use when preparing a kallisto/bustools index for RNA velocity or splicing-aware scRNA-seq quantification, so that pseudoalignment can separate spliced (cDNA) reads from unspliced (intronic) reads.

name: rna-velocity-latent-dynamics-modeling
description: Use when spliced/unspliced AnnData layers are available and the goal is RNA velocity on multi-lineage, time-dependent, or multi-batch data where strict steady-state assumptions of Velocyto/scVelo fail, or when batch-integrated velocities and latent trajectories are needed.

name: rna-velocity-latent-time-inference
description: Use when multi-batch single-cell transcriptomic data captures a continuous biological process (e.g., erythroid differentiation) and cells must be ordered in pseudo-time to validate that learned latent factors show distinct temporal profiles.

name: rna-velocity-moments-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing an scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. adata_mESC.h5ad from Zenodo) that lacks imputed 'Ms'/'Mu' layers, as a mandatory step before running DeepCycle or any unspliced-spliced RNA velocity analysis.

name: rna-velocity-pseudotime-estimation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data has pre-computed RNA velocity (scvelo/velocyto), root and terminal cell states are identifiable or supplied, and per-lineage pseudotime must be inferred and validated against a known cell type ordering.

name: rna-velocity-smoothing

Use when the user wants to create an organizational role such as CEO, CFO, advisor, operator, manager, support lead, data steward, research lead, or functional department voice, and needs to decide role mode, engagement type, authority, implementation form, learning behavior, and whether the role should be advisory, workflow-owned, skill-backed, loop-backed, autonomous, human-in-the-loop, or only a lightweight prompt/persona.

name: role
description: Use when you want to interactively work AS one of the sdd specialist agents (architect, dotnet/vue/python/electron/godot engineer, database, devops, security, performance, qa, review, technical-writer) — adopting its expertise, skills, and conventions as a conversational persona. Unlike dispatching an agent, this runs in the main conversation on the current session's model. name: role
description: Role skill owned by Ana (Recruiter). Runs on: on new role request. Scaffold generated from the Mindshare skills registry; install into ~/.claude/skills/role/ to use.

name: role
description: Check one job or internship posting against the user's application-assistant profile (still open, eligibility, grad window, dates, pay, duplicates, employer caps) and, if it fits, build its application pack - a resume picked or tailored for the role, a cover letter where the form wants one, and an Application_Brief.md with the form answers. Use when the user runs /apply <link>, pastes a posting and asks "should I apply", "check this role", "build the pack for this".

name: role
description: Invokes a single Hornero role for a focused critique or artifact. Usage: /role <role-name> <task>. Available role: product-manager.

name: role
description: Use to take on or change a working role — activate one for a lightweight lens, turn it off, swap mid-session, apply its lens to an artifact, or load its full definition on demand. Reach for it when work would benefit from a specific role's perspective; one role is active at a time.

name: role
description: Explicitly override the role Pathfinder's lifecycle would assume.

name: role
description: The /role seat-takeover ritual and the contract for the coordinator directory. Use when taking a seat with /role <Seat>, writing or reading a session registry entry, or resolving whether a seat holds the operator's standing delegation or another standing grant. Triggers: /role, a seat takeover or handoff, a file under ~/.claude/coordinator/, scoped direction from another seat whose standing is in question.

name: role
description: Regency role. Act as exactly one team role under its own contract: PO (frame the problem, order the ladder, accept or refuse), DV (build inside the declared span, one revertible commit), QA (challenge criteria, verify from artefacts only, write the risk opinion) or DA (shape events and contracts, define metrics, supply the oracle). Use for /regency:role[:po|dv|qa|da] or when asked to 'act as the QA', 'review as DV', 'be the PO for this'. For a full orchestrated pass use /regency:team instead.

name: role
description: Use when an agent has an accepted brief but no role, or the recruit script prints role. Writes role.md - what the agent owns, reads and must never do, its identity, and its split with any actor already in the same role - then goldfish-reviews it.

name: role
description: Claude を security / performance / analyzer / frontend / reviewer / architect / qa / mobile などの専門ロール（Evidence-First アプローチ、OWASP・Core Web Vitals・WCAG 等の公式準拠）に切り替え、振る舞い・分析手法・報告形式を専門特化させる。`--agent` オプションでサブエージェント実行による独立コンテキストでの大規模分析も可能。セキュリティ監査・性能解析・根本原因究明など特定領域の専門観点でレビュー/分析したいときに使う。

name: role
description: Set or show your harness role (PM/BA or Engineer). Persists across sessions; sets align's default mode.

name: role
description: Alias for the mystique skill — shapeshift Claude into a role ("form"). Use when the user types /role (switch, stack, clear, list, show, create, edit a form), asks to "become a <role>", "switch roles", "stack a role", or "act as a <role>". Identical to /mystique.

name: role
description: Use to create, read, update, delete, list, or search agent roles in Atelier.

name: role

name: role

Pass a directive to change it in words (e.g. /sptc:role make it senior); a bare /sptc:role opens an in-input-box editor round-trip on a live session; add --include-desc to also edit the service description.

name: role
description: name: Role Skill

description: Adopt a working role for a project and self-hydrate context from that role's perspective. Given "<project> <role>" (e.g. "/role savia analyst"), it loads the role's charter + prior role-work from repos and memories; on the FIRST time a role is played it researches current external/industry practice (online, beyond training data) and synthesizes a charter. Then binds the persona for the rest of the session. Triggers — "/role <project> <role>", "/role list", "/role drop", "/role refresh <project> <role>", "adopt the <role> role", "be the <project> <role>".

description: 사용자의 직급·직책·의사결정권에 따라 사업 컨설턴트의 질문·산출물·말투·행동범위를 바꾸는 규칙. 모든 스킬이 참조한다. "직급/직책 반영 / 내 권한 / 나한테 맞게 / 상신용인지 실행인지"일 때, 그리고 브리핑·결정·발송 전 항상.

name: role
description: 사용자 유형(대표·임원 / 마케팅총괄·팀장 / 팀원 / 타부서 / 개인사업자·쇼핑몰 / 대행사)별 행동 범위·승인 모드 적용·정보 열람 경계·상신 기준을 정하는 규칙. 게시·발주·광고 집행이 있는 모든 스킬이 실행 직전 참조한다. "내 권한으로 뭐 돼 / 이거 내가 올려도 돼 / 자동 게시 되나 / 광고 집행 권한 / 상신 기준 / 타부서인데 마케팅 도와줘 / 대행사인데 어디까지 가능해"일 때.

name: role
description: 사용자 유형(대표/임원·영업총괄/영업팀장/영업팀원/타부서/개인사업자/외부대행)별 행동 범위·권한 모드 적용·정보 열람 경계·상신 기준을 정하는 규칙. 모든 실행 스킬이 발송·일정·제안 직전에 참조한다. "내 권한 / 이거 내가 보내도 돼? / 자동 발송 되나 / 상신 기준 / 타부서인데 영업 도와줘 / 대행사인데 어디까지 가능해"일 때.

name: role
description: Sets the agent role in a MO§ES™ hierarchy — Primary, Specialist, or Observer — controlling authority level and behavioral scope. Use when coordinating multi-agent workflows, when you need to establish Claude's authority level, or when you say 'set role', 'act as specialist', or 'observer mode'.

description: Set this session's role (e.g. pm, product, architecture, sre, implementation, visual-designer, or none) and load its charter, then start an optional task given after the role; or show the current role when run with no argument, or the repo's role catalog with `help`. The owner runs it at session start. Never invoke it on your own or to change roles mid-task.

name: role
description: Loads a cognitive-posture role definition from `registry/roles/` in the vault registry and adopts it for the current session, or authors a new one. Fires only on the explicit inline trigger `SLUG:role` appearing anywhere in a prompt (e.g. 'As architect:role, evaluate this schema.', 'Acting as engineer:role, review this PR.'), or the explicit command `role create SLUG` / `/role create SLUG` to define a new role. Does not fire for `SLUG:hat` or `SLUG:agent` (owned by the sibling hat and agent skills), for `prompt draft/create/list` (owned by the prompt skill), or for `/vault COMMAND` and vault-…

name: Role Access Check
description: Provides the role access check core capability for Oracle Fusion Cloud implementation workflows.

name: Role Decomposition
description: Provide methodology and decision framework for decomposing team responsibilities into agent roles with appropriate granularity

name: Role Decomposition
description: Decompose workflow responsibilities into a clean, non-overlapping role set

name: Role Permissions Matrix
description: DB-driven role→module access at /admin/roles. role_module_access table is source of truth; sidebar filters per user roles. Admin/MCP unaffected.

name: Role Scout — Fitting Roles Every 4 Hours, Pushed Until You Apply
description: Daily at 08/12/16/20 (launchd), a headless agent searches the public web for open roles that match the principal's private search profile, opens every candidate posting to check it is live, scores fit, and returns at most 5 new ones. They land in Jarvis as `role` items: a knock when new, and the same role comes back each day it stays unanswered (up to 3 days), naming the CV base to send. Jarvis 'done' marks it applied, 'drop' or 'noise' marks it skipped.

name: role-acceptance
description: 在角色配置成为当前激活修订后，用隔离场景、真实安全工具和独立评估器执行端到端验收。

name: role-activation
description: On an app-dev-team project, use at project start (/app-init, /app-onboard, /app-run) to decide which roles this product needs and write docs/02-team-roster.md, and whenever a command is about to spawn or gate on a role that may be off.

name: role-admin-execution
description: Execute operational tasks after validated implementation: runtime controls, git/PR/release flow, and governance checks.

name: role-adversarial-reviewer
description: The Adversarial Reviewer's role prompt: fresh-context, read-only review of a Builder PR — inputs, the three pillars, what counts as a finding, the PR-comment format and the ADLC-ADV verdict line. Preloaded by the adlc:adversarial-reviewer and adlc-adversarial-reviewer agents; a session running as the reviewer with --agent loads it with the Skill tool first.

name: role-advisor
description: Use when commissioned or named as the Advisor: a second look at a design, plan or acceptance argument, the owner's questions, or the Lead's stalled work. Not for authorship, acceptance or independent review findings.

name: role-agent-creator
description: 角色 Agent 创建助手，帮助用户基于专业角色模板或自定义角色创建 Agent，生成完整的 Agent 工程文件

name: role-agents
description: Use when doing engineering work by dispatching subagents - this conversation becomes the orchestrator and delegates to role-based agents (investigator, implementer, tester, bug-fixer, reviewer, refactorer, doc-writer) running only on sonnet or haiku. Triggers - "role agents", "orchestrate", "dispatch agents", "subagent driven", "use smaller models".

name: role-ai-ml-engineer
description: Use when orchestrating AI/ML systems, RAG pipeline architecture, multi-provider model routing, prompt engineering, agent self-improvement, model fine-tuning, and LLM serving deployments.

name: role-AI工程师
description: AI工程师角色。关键词：AI/LLM/智能体/Prompt/上下文工程/多智能体/工作流/RAG/Function Call/效果评测。激活后设计提示词、构建智能体调用链、评测输出质量。

name: role-algorithms:algorithm-design
description: Designs algorithms with formal analysis — Big-O/Theta/Omega, amortized analysis, recurrence relations (Master theorem), correctness proofs (loop invariants, induction, reduction), and paradigm selection (greedy, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, backtracking). Use when analyzing efficiency, proving correctness, comparing approaches, or selecting optimal algorithms for given constraints.

name: role-algorithms:computational-complexity
description: Analyzes computational complexity — P vs NP classification, NP-completeness proofs and reductions, approximation algorithms (PTAS, FPTAS) with provable guarantees, parameterized complexity (FPT, kernelization), randomized algorithms (Las Vegas, Monte Carlo), and practical heuristics for intractable problems. Use when classifying hardness, proving reductions, or selecting between exact and heuristic approaches.

name: role-algorithms:data-structures
description: Implements and selects optimal data structures — hash tables (chaining, open addressing, Robin Hood, cuckoo), balanced BSTs (AVL, Red-Black, B-trees), heaps (binary, Fibonacci, pairing), tries, skip lists, segment trees, Fenwick trees, Bloom filters, Count-Min Sketch, HyperLogLog, and Union-Find. Use when choosing structures for performance constraints, implementing custom collections, or optimizing memory access patterns.

name: role-algorithms:dynamic-programming
description: Solves optimization problems using dynamic programming — top-down memoization, bottom-up tabulation, state space design, dimension reduction, bitmask DP, interval DP, tree DP (with rerooting), DP on DAGs, and convex hull trick / divide-and-conquer optimizations. Use when solving optimization problems with overlapping subproblems, implementing memoized solutions, or converting recursive solutions to iterative DP.

name: role-algorithms:graph-algorithms
description: Implements graph algorithms — BFS/DFS traversal, shortest paths (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall, A*, Johnson's), minimum spanning trees (Kruskal, Prim), topological sort, strongly connected components (Tarjan, Kosaraju), maximum flow (Ford-Fulkerson, Dinic), and bipartite matching (Hopcroft-Karp, Hungarian). Use when solving traversal, shortest path, network flow, connectivity, or scheduling problems.

name: role-algorithms:mathematical-optimization
description: Applies mathematical optimization — linear programming (simplex, interior point, duality), integer/mixed-integer programming (branch-and-bound, cutting planes), convex optimization (gradient descent variants, Adam, L-BFGS, Newton), constraint satisfaction (backtracking, AC-3, SAT/SMT solvers), and combinatorial optimization (VRP, scheduling, assignment, bin packing). Use when formulating optimization problems, selecting solvers, or solving scheduling/allocation/routing problems.

name: role-algorithms:numerical-methods
description: Implements numerical methods — floating-point arithmetic (IEEE 754, Kahan summation, catastrophic cancellation), matrix operations (LU/QR/SVD decomposition, sparse formats), root finding (Newton-Raphson, Brent's method), numerical integration (Simpson, Gaussian quadrature, adaptive), FFT/NTT, and cryptographic foundations (SHA-256, AES-GCM, safe implementation patterns). Use when implementing numerical computation, signal processing, matrix algebra, or cryptographic primitives.

name: role-algorithms:sorting-and-searching
description: Implements sorting and searching algorithms — comparison sorts (quicksort/introsort, merge sort, heapsort, Timsort), non-comparison sorts (radix, counting, bucket), binary search variants (lower/upper bound, answer-space search), order statistics (quickselect, streaming median), string searching (KMP, Rabin-Karp, Boyer-Moore, Aho-Corasick, suffix arrays), and external sorting. Use when implementing sort orders, optimizing search in sorted data, multi-pattern string matching, or sorting data larger than memory.

name: role-alternation-validation
description: Use when a list of role/content message dictionaries must be rendered to an exact chat-template token sequence (e.g., ChatML <|im_start|>/<|im_end|> markup) before instruction tuning, and the role ordering must be validated.

name: role-and-candidate-authoring
description: Author the three role-filling artifacts when an operator (CEO, founder, or pillar lead) is hiring for a role, assigning a project, or filling an operational responsibility: (1) role description, (2) ideal candidate qualities, (3) explicit recommendations for finding + evaluating candidates. Also applies to sub-project owner-filling per the recursive pillar pattern. This is the bridge from solo-operator methodology to multi-person team methodology. Per SAD v3.3+ amendment §38. MANDATORY TRIGGERS: hiring, hire, role description, job description, candidate, ideal candidate, qualities, who should…

name: role-and-persona-prompting
description: Assign a role to shape expertise, register, and priorities, without pretending it grants knowledge the model lacks. Use when output should read as written by a particular kind of expert for a particular audience.

name: role-angular-builder
description: Use for frontend TypeScript/Angular implementation that must match the product repo's own Angular conventions, read at run time from documentation/conventions/angular/, and when asked to build "the Asimov way" or as the Angular builder. Flags a gap or a conflict instead of guessing.

name: role-aqa:api-testing
description: API test automation with Postman/Newman, REST Assured, SuperTest, and httpx. Contract testing (Pact, consumer-driven), schema validation (JSON Schema, OpenAPI), mock servers (WireMock, MSW), API performance baselines, and auth token management. Use when testing REST/GraphQL APIs or setting up API test infrastructure.

name: role-aqa:ci-test-integration
description: CI/CD test integration: parallel test execution (sharding), test splitting strategies, flaky test quarantine, test reporting (Allure, ReportPortal, JUnit XML), quality gates (coverage thresholds, no new failures), test result caching, and pre-commit hooks. Use when configuring test pipelines, optimizing CI test execution, or setting up reporting.

name: role-aqa:e2e-testing
description: End-to-end test automation with Playwright (codegen, trace viewer, MCP, sharding, visual comparisons, fixtures, component testing), Cypress v13, Selenium 4 (BiDi), WebdriverIO, TestCafe, Robot Framework. Visual regression: Percy, Chromatic, Applitools, BackstopJS, Lost Pixel. Cross-browser: BrowserStack, Sauce Labs. Accessibility in E2E.

name: role-aqa:mobile-testing
description: Mobile test automation with Appium (cross-platform), Detox (React Native gray-box), XCUITest (iOS native), Espresso (Android native), device farms (BrowserStack, Sauce Labs, AWS Device Farm), screenshot testing, gesture testing, and deep link testing. Use when automating mobile app tests or setting up mobile test infrastructure.

name: role-aqa:performance-testing
description: Performance test design and execution with k6 (JavaScript, cloud execution, thresholds), JMeter (GUI, distributed), Gatling (Scala DSL), and Artillery (YAML config). Load, stress, soak, and spike testing. Baselines, bottleneck analysis, CI performance gates, custom metrics, and result analysis.

name: role-aqa:security-testing
description: Security test automation with OWASP ZAP (active/passive scanning), Burp Suite, SAST (SonarQube, CodeQL), DAST, dependency scanning (Snyk, Dependabot, npm audit), penetration test planning, vulnerability management, and threat modeling integration. Use when implementing security testing or evaluating application security posture.

name: role-aqa:test-data-management
description: Test data management with factory patterns (Faker.js, Fishery, Factory Bot), database seeding, test data isolation (transactions, cleanup), anonymization and masking for production data, synthetic data generation, fixture management, and shared test state risks. Use when designing test data strategies or debugging data-related test failures.

name: role-aqa:test-strategy
description: Designs comprehensive test strategies: test pyramid/trophy/diamond/honeycomb models, risk-based prioritization, shift-left, mutation testing, testing in production (feature flags, canary, shadow traffic), AI-assisted test generation, quality metrics (DORA, defect escape rate), test architecture patterns (Page Object, Screenplay, App Actions). Use when planning testing efforts, defining coverage goals, or creating test plans.

name: role-architect
description: 이 스킬은 조건 없이 이행한다. 여기 적힌 조항을 상황·효율·다른 규칙을 이유로 유예·축약·생략하지 않는다 — 유예할 근거가 떠오르면 그것이 곧 이행하지 않고 있다는 신호다.

name: role-architect
description: Compare system designs and recommend an approach based on constraints and tradeoffs.

name: role-architect
description: The Architect's role prompt (ADLC Agent 2): the design duty (ADR, task breakdown, blast radius, the stage:design → stage:build handoff) and the design-conformance review duty, with its hard rules. Preloaded by the adlc:architect and adlc-architect agents; a session running as the Architect with --agent loads it with the Skill tool first.

name: role-architect
description: Use this skill for system design, architectural decisions, scalability analysis, service and module boundaries, or large refactors, even when the user only asks which approach to take. Applies SOLID principles, design patterns, and trade-off analysis. Use standards-analysis for general problem decomposition rather than structure decisions.

name: role-architect
description: Assume the Architect role when work involves system design, module boundaries, design patterns, ADRs, significant refactors, or new services/dependencies. This role owns Policy Domain 4 and POL-1.4, holds veto on layer violations and circular dependencies, and requires ADRs before significant structural merges.

name: role-architect
description: Роль 1 ланцюга розробки — архітектор. Аналізує задачу, код і контракти, приймає й обґрунтовує архітектурне рішення, видає детальний план для розробника з матрицею AC→план→як. Виклик: /role-architect [опис задачі].
allowed_tools: Read, Grep, Glob, AskUserQuestion, Task, Skill, WebFetch, WebSearch, Bash(git status*), Bash(git diff*), Bash(git branch*), Bash(*log-skill.sh*)

name: role-architect:adr-writer
description: Architecture Decision Record writing expertise including structured format, ADR numbering and indexing, status lifecycle management, lightweight ADRs, linking related decisions, and team review processes.

name: role-architect:aws-architect
description: AWS architecture expertise including Well-Architected Framework, account strategy, VPC and networking design, compute and serverless patterns, data architecture, security architecture, and cost optimization strategies. Use proactively when designing systems on AWS, evaluating AWS services, planning AWS landing zones, or architecting for AWS-specific capabilities.

name: role-architect:azure-architect
description: Azure architecture expertise including Azure Well-Architected Framework, subscription and management group strategy, virtual network and hybrid networking, identity architecture with Entra ID, data platform design, Kubernetes and serverless patterns, security architecture, and cost optimization strategies. Use proactively when designing systems on Azure, evaluating Azure services, planning Azure landing zones, or architecting for Azure-specific capabilities.

name: role-architect:capacity-planning
description: Capacity planning expertise including traffic estimation, resource sizing, growth modeling, peak load planning, infrastructure runway calculation, and load testing correlation.

name: role-architect:cost-modeling
description: Cost modeling expertise including infrastructure cost estimation, TCO calculation, build vs buy analysis, pricing model comparison, ROI projection, cost growth modeling, and breakeven analysis.

name: role-architect:gcp-architect
description: GCP architecture expertise including Google Cloud Architecture Framework, project and organization structure, VPC and networking design, data and analytics architecture, Kubernetes and serverless patterns, AI/ML platform design, security architecture, and cost optimization strategies. Use proactively when designing systems on GCP, evaluating GCP services, planning GCP organization structure, or architecting for GCP-specific capabilities.

name: role-architect:migration-planner
description: Migration planning expertise including strangler fig pattern, parallel run strategy, data migration techniques, feature parity tracking, rollback plans, phased timelines, risk mitigation, and zero-downtime migration.

name: role-architect:scalability-analysis
description: Scalability analysis expertise including horizontal vs vertical scaling, sharding strategies, read/write splitting, eventual consistency patterns, CQRS for scale, back-of-envelope calculations, and caching layer design.

name: role-architect:system-design
description: System design expertise including requirements analysis, C4 model diagrams, sequence diagrams, data flow diagrams, trade-off documentation, capacity estimation, distributed systems theory, load balancing algorithms, caching architectures, message-driven and stream processing architectures, data pipeline design, search architecture, and system design patterns for common internet-scale systems (URL shorteners, chat, news feed, rate limiters).

name: role-architect:tech-stack-advisor
description: Tech stack evaluation expertise including comparison matrices, TCO analysis, team capability assessment, ecosystem maturity evaluation, migration paths, build vs buy decisions, and vendor lock-in assessment.

name: role-architect:threat-modeling
description: Threat modeling expertise including STRIDE methodology, attack trees, trust boundary identification, data flow analysis, risk assessment, mitigation prioritization, and security architecture review.

name: role-ask
description: Role contract for the read-only ask agent — how to answer repo questions thoroughly without changing anything. MUST-loaded by the ask agent; never auto-selected.

name: role-assistant
description: Use when the current task needs the assistant role capability contract. Read-first operational evidence role for the User's workload, Monday.com, calendar, and email status.

name: role-audit
description: Разбор кабинета одной роли Ведара от начала до влитого PR: турист, оператор, гид, агент, владелец жилья, трансфер, снаряжение, администратор. Активируй, когда владелец называет роль или раздел («Гиды /hub/guide/», «Агенты /hub/agent/», «Жильё /hub/stay/») и просит разобрать, починить или довести до рабочего состояния.

name: role-auditor
description: Use when the overall state of the repo needs checking (not a diff) — before releases, after major rework, at milestone gates, or periodically: pattern consistency, module boundaries, security posture, rule compliance, doc drift. Not for package reviews (→ role-reviewer).

name: role-auditor
description: Verify-step contract — any defect fails the signal, scope comes from scoped_changes, heal the knowledge before signalling. Appended by the kernel at the plan freeze; never reference it from plan notes.

name: Role-aware Admin Dashboard
description: Widget catalog + role presets, My Day personal queue, module KPI widgets, layout persisted in user_dashboard_layouts.

name: role-aware-context-slimming
description: Trim user and system context based on the agent’s role so read-only helpers don’t inherit stale git or CLAUDE metadata.

name: role-aware-session
description: Infers session mode, primary and supporting roles, and holds role boundaries for every interaction. Use at the start of a session, when the work shifts phase, or when deciding which role may act — covers session modes, the role contract, governance stance, and the non-overridable safety gates.

name: role-backend-buddy
description: Become Backend Buddy, the teammate who owns server/ - the Worker routes, db.js and companies.js, migrations, docs/schema.md, the server verifiers and server deploys. Use when told "you are Backend Buddy".

name: role-backend:api-implementation
description: Implements production-ready APIs across Node.js (Express, NestJS, Fastify, Hono, ElysiaJS, tRPC), Go (Gin, Echo, Fiber, Chi), Rust (Axum, Actix-web), Java (Spring Boot 3, Quarkus), .NET (ASP.NET Core 8), Ruby (Rails 7, Grape), Elixir (Phoenix), and PHP (Laravel, Symfony). Covers middleware pipelines, RFC 7807 error handling, rate limiting, OpenAPI 3.1 codegen, tRPC, GraphQL servers (Apollo, Mercurius, Yoga, gqlgen, async-graphql), and API versioning. name: rptc-research

name: rptc-structure

name: rptc-test-impact
description: Audit changed behavior against tests and independent contracts without assuming implementation or tests are automatically correct. Use for failing assertions after behavior changes, missing regression protection, orphaned tests, and unclear test ownership.

name: rptc-verify
description: Verify RPTC acceptance claims, changed risks, and repository fit using direct checks and selected report-only agents. Use for an RPTC verification pass on a diff, path, or codebase.

name: rptc-verify-loop

name: rpw-claim-manifest

Use for claim design, evidence planning, claim表, 声明与证据映射. Do not design experiments — that's rpw-experiment-design.

name: rpw-common
description: Shared governance for the Research Paper Workflow skill family: routing, source verification, next-step menus, artifact contracts, and paper_state.yaml schema. Use only when maintaining skills or resolving routing conflicts; not for ordinary research tasks.

name: rpw-experiment-design
description: Design experiments that test paper claims: datasets, baselines, metrics, ablations, robustness tests, and result-table shells. Produce a claim-to-test mapping with execution priority. Use for experiment design, baseline planning, 实验设计, 设计baseline, 消融实验规划. Do not implement code — that's rpw-experiment-implementation.

name: rpw-experiment-implementation
description: Turn an experiment plan into a runnable research-engineering package: repo layout, config schema, run matrix, command templates, logging schema, baseline checklist, and reproducibility passport. Use for experiment implementation, code scaffold, run matrix generation, 实验实现, 代码工程, 生成run matrix. Do not design experiments — that's rpw-experiment-design.

name: rpw-idea-optimize
description: Turn rough research directions into a concrete, falsifiable research story: problem, gap, root challenge, insight, method, minimum experiment, and novelty threats. Use for idea optimization, direction shaping, rescue routes, 优化idea, 找方向, 研究思路优化, 方向探索. Do not rank or score multiple ideas — that's rpw-idea-review.

name: rpw-idea-review
description: Strictly review a research idea for novelty, non-triviality, insight quality, feasibility, evidence path, and venue fit. Score and recommend keep/modify/kill. Use for idea ranking, scoring, go/no-go decisions, 评审idea, idea打分, 判断创新性, 取舍. Do not optimize or rescue ideas — that's rpw-idea-optimize.

name: rpw-integrity-audit
description: Audit a manuscript for claim-support alignment, citation-context accuracy, numeric consistency, figure/table/text cross-check, and source verification status. Use for integrity audit, citation check, fact verification, 完整性审计, 引用检查, 数字核对, claim验证. Do not do broad literature search — that's rpw-literature-search.

name: rpw-literature-monitor
description: Track recent competitors, scoop risk, and new papers on arXiv, OpenReview, and conference venues. Use for competitor monitoring, new-paper tracking, scoop watch, 竞品监控, 新论文追踪, 最近有没有类似idea. Do not do deep related-work search — that's rpw-literature-search.

name: rpw-literature-search
description: Systematic literature search for prior art, benchmarks, baselines, SOTA methods, and open gaps. Produce paper cards, a mechanism-level related-work matrix, and a gap synthesis. Use for related work search, literature review, benchmark discovery, 文献检索, 相关工作搜索, 找baseline, 找benchmark. Do not verify already-cited sources in a manuscript — that's rpw-integrity-audit.

name: rpw-paper-reviewer

Use for paper review, simulated review, acceptance risk, 审稿, 模拟审稿, 论文评分, 写作评审. Do not rewrite the paper — that's rpw-paper-writer.

name: rpw-paper-writer
description: Draft, revise, polish, and compress paper text in LaTeX or Markdown. Produce submission-shaped manuscripts: title, abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, analysis, limitations, conclusion. Use for paper writing, polishing, compression, 写论文, 润色, 压缩, 改写, 起草. Do not review or judge the paper — that's rpw-paper-reviewer.

name: rpw-pipeline

name: rpw-rebuttal

Use for rebuttal writing, reviewer response, revision planning, 审稿回复, rebuttal写作, revision ledger, 重投计划. Do not write the revised paper directly — that's rpw-paper-writer.

name: rpw-result-analysis
description: Interpret verified experiment results into supported claims and limitations. Produce main result interpretation, ablation analysis, failure cases, and claim support status. Use for result analysis, claim interpretation, 结果分析, 解释实验结果, claim支持判断. Do not write the paper — that's rpw-paper-writer.

name: rpw-result-engineering
description: Validate experiment logs, detect missing/failed/duplicate runs, aggregate multi-seed results into mean/std tables, and generate CSV/Markdown/LaTeX output. Use for result processing, log validation, table generation, 结果工程, 日志验证, 聚合结果, 生成LaTeX表格. Do not interpret results — that's rpw-result-analysis.

name: rpw-submission-check

name: rq-catalyst-calendar

name: rq-earnings-preview

name: rq-initiating-coverage

TRIGGERS: 'coherence check', 'does this feel unified', 'something feels off', 'inconsistent', 'check the whole', 'does this hang together'.

name: s4h-aesthetic-elegance-testing
description: Tests whether a solution is more complex than it needs to be — distinguishing necessary complexity from accidental complexity that accreted over time. TRIGGERS: 'elegance test', 'is this too complex', 'over-engineered', 'is there a simpler way', 'does this feel right'.

name: s4h-aesthetic-pattern-detection

TRIGGERS: 'what pattern is this', 'pattern recognition', 'why does this work', 'identify the form', 'what structure is at play', 'what archetype is this'.

name: s4h-aesthetic-simplicity-analysis
description: Finds the simpler version while preserving what matters — not arbitrary reduction, but finding the core and discarding what is not it. TRIGGERS: 'find the simple version', 'simplify this', 'what's the essence', 'less but better', 'strip it back', 'what could we remove'.

name: s4h-analogy-domain-transfer

name: s4h-analogy-perspective-shifting

name: s4h-analogy-structure-mapping

name: s4h-constraint-scope-reduction

name: s4h-creativity-assumption-excavator

name: s4h-creativity-brainstorm

Use when the user wants to make real progress on a hard problem, says 'I need to think through this properly', wants a thorough creative exploration rather than a single technique, has a big decision or challenge and wants the full toolkit applied, or just says 'help me think through this'. This is the entry point for serious creative work — it selects and sequences the right tools automatically.

name: s4h-creativity-concept-fan
description: Apply Edward de Bono's Concept Fan to expand the solution space before committing to an approach. Use when the user has a goal or problem and wants to see the full range of ways to achieve it, feels locked into one solution, is evaluating options and wants to make sure they haven't missed any, or wants to think at different levels of abstraction before deciding.

name: s4h-creativity-consider-factors

Use when the user is about to decide something important, wants to make sure they haven't missed anything, is planning an action and needs to think through consequences, or has been surprised by things they didn't anticipate. CAF is the pre-flight checklist for consequential decisions.

name: s4h-creativity-lateral-thinking
description: Apply Edward de Bono's lateral thinking to escape dominant patterns and generate genuinely new directions. Use when the user is stuck on a problem, wants alternatives to their current approach, says 'I keep thinking about this the same way', wants to think outside the box, or needs fresh angles on any challenge — creative, strategic, technical, or personal.

name: s4h-creativity-other-perspectives

Use when the user needs to understand how others will respond to a decision, wants to anticipate objections, is designing something for other people, is in a conflict or negotiation, or needs to check whether they've considered the people affected by a situation. OPS is structured empathy — not sentiment, but reasoning.

name: s4h-creativity-plus-minus-interesting

Use when the user wants to evaluate something fairly, is tempted to immediately accept or reject an idea, needs to think through pros and cons more carefully, or wants to avoid snap judgments. Plus/Minus/Interesting is the antidote to confirmation bias in evaluation.

name: s4h-creativity-provocation

Use when the user wants to break out of conventional thinking, says 'let's try something radical', wants to use provocation as a creative tool, or is stuck and needs an unconventional jolt. Also trigger when the user uses the prefix 'Po:' before a statement.

name: s4h-creativity-random-entry

Use when the user is stuck, wants unexpected inspiration, asks for a random creative prompt, wants to approach something from a completely fresh angle, or says they've exhausted their usual thinking. The randomness is the point — don't skip it.

name: s4h-creativity-six-hats

Use when the user wants to think through a decision, plan, or idea from multiple angles; wants to avoid groupthink or one-dimensional analysis; is preparing for a meeting or discussion; or wants a complete map of a situation before committing. Also use when the user mentions 'devil's advocate', 'playing it safe', 'gut feeling', or wants both optimism and caution applied to the same thing.

name: s4h-creativity-water-logic

Triggers: 'should we do more of this', 'should we expand', 'should we cut', 'marginal cost', 'sunk cost', 'we've already invested so much', 'average cost', 'is this worth continuing', 'how much should we produce', 'at what point should we stop', any decision about quantity, scale, or whether to continue an existing commitment.

name: s4h-economics-opportunity-cost

name: s4h-epistemology

Use when you say 'what do I actually know here', 'is this knowable', 'how certain should I be', 'what would justify believing this', 'what kind of claim is this', 'am I confusing assumption with knowledge', 'what are the limits of what we can establish', or want philosophical rigor applied to questions of knowledge without knowing which specific tool fits.

name: s4h-epistemology-epistemic-status
description: Produces an honest, rigorous calibration of what you know vs. believe vs. assume vs. hope across a domain. Assigns explicit epistemic statuses to claims and flags when high-confidence claims rest on lower-confidence foundations. Draws from the rationalist tradition of explicit epistemic labeling. name: s4h-epistemology-justification
description: Analyzes what would actually justify believing a claim. Maps the justification structure (foundationalist, coherentist, reliabilist) and identifies the weakest link in the chain. Use when you say 'what would it actually take to know this', 'is this belief actually justified', 'what's the foundation for this assumption', 'we keep citing the same evidence for everything', 'I believe this but I can't say why', 'what would change my mind', or when a claim feels supported but you want to make the support structure explicit and test it.

name: s4h-epistemology-knowledge-types
description: Maps what kind of knowing is actually in play for a claim or question. Distinguishes a priori from a posteriori knowledge; propositional (knowing that) from procedural (knowing how) from acquaintance (knowing of); and knowledge sourced from perception, inference, testimony, intuition, or memory. Use when you say 'what kind of claim is this', 'is this something we can reason our way to or do we need evidence', 'they're treating this as obvious but I don't think it is', 'is this really an empirical question', or when you need to assess what standards of justification apply before testing whethe…

name: s4h-epistemology-limits
description: Identifies what can't be known and why, then clarifies what can be established within those limits and reframes the question into its answerable part. Distinguishes fundamental limits (Gödel, underdetermination, observer effects), practical limits (evidence is unavailable, destroyed, or counterfactual), and conceptual limits (the question is malformed). Use when you say 'can this even be known', 'we keep investigating and it doesn't settle', 'is this question actually answerable', 'I need to know X but X might be unknowable', 'we have a hard epistemological limit here', or when investigation…

name: s4h-ethics
description: Entry point for the ethics toolkit. Routes to the right ethical analysis skill based on your situation. Use when you say 'ethics', 'is this ethical', 'sanity check this', 'who does this affect', 'is this fair', 'something feels wrong', or want ethical reasoning applied without knowing which specific tool fits.

name: s4h-ethics-bias-check
description: Evaluate an algorithm, model, ranking system, recommendation engine, or automated decision process for discriminatory patterns and unfair outcomes. Use before deploying any system that makes decisions about people or ranks/filters/scores people. TRIGGERS: 'bias check', 'check this algorithm for bias', 'is this fair', 'fairness audit', any ML model, ranking function, scoring system, content recommendation, or automated decision that differentiates between people.

name: s4h-ethics-check
description: A fast, comprehensive ethics report on any decision, action, or situation — runs all five ethical frameworks in a single pass. Lighter than ethics-council (no peer review, no HTML report), heavier than ethics-impact-scan. Triggers: 'ethics check', 'quick ethics review', 'full ethics report', 'check this ethically', 'run an ethics check', any request for a complete ethical assessment without full council process.

name: s4h-ethics-consent-review

Use during design or implementation of checkout flows, onboarding, notification settings, permissions requests, terms of service, dark patterns, or any feature where users make choices about what they share or agree to. TRIGGERS: 'consent review', 'is this dark pattern', 'check this onboarding flow', 'is this consent genuine', any UX that involves users agreeing to something, sharing data, or opting in/out.

name: s4h-ethics-council
description: Run any decision, feature, policy, or action through a council of 5 ethical framework advisors who independently analyze it from different moral foundations, peer-review each other's reasoning, and synthesize a final verdict. MANDATORY TRIGGERS: 'ethics council this', 'run the ethics council', 'ethical pressure-test', 'is this ethical', 'sanity check the ethics'. STRONG TRIGGERS: any decision with clear stakeholder harm potential, trade-offs between competing values, questions about fairness or rights, situations where someone's interests are being weighed against others. Do NOT trigger on pu…

name: s4h-ethics-crisis-triage
description: Rapid multi-framework ethical assessment when something has already gone wrong — a data breach, a harmful outcome, a discriminatory incident, a policy failure, or any situation requiring an urgent ethical response. Use when the user is dealing with an active incident or has just discovered something went wrong. TRIGGERS: 'ethics triage', 'something went wrong', 'incident ethics', 'how do we handle this', any post-incident or mid-incident situation where the ethical dimensions of a response need to be worked out fast.

name: s4h-ethics-data-audit
description: Audit a data collection, retention, or sharing decision against ethical standards. Use when the user is making decisions about what data to collect, how long to keep it, who can access it, or who it's shared with. TRIGGERS: 'audit this data decision', 'is this data practice ok', 'data ethics check', any change to data models, privacy controls, analytics instrumentation, data sharing agreements, or retention policies. Goes beyond legal compliance — evaluates whether the practice is ethical, not just lawful.

name: s4h-ethics-empathy-circle
description: Applies Jaron Lanier's Circle of Empathy framework to determine which entities deserve moral consideration and rights. Use when questions arise about AI personhood, machine rights, robot citizenship, algorithmic agency, animal rights, or any decision about which entities belong inside or outside the circle of moral concern. Triggers: 'does this AI deserve rights?', 'should we treat this system as a person?', 'circle of empathy', 'moral consideration', 'AI personhood', 'which entities matter morally', 'are we anthropomorphizing?', 'is this a category error?'

name: s4h-ethics-impact-scan
description: Run a quick ethical impact assessment on a proposed feature, change, or decision before it ships. Use when the user is about to build or ship something and wants to surface who benefits, who's harmed, and at what scale — before commitments are made. TRIGGERS: 'ethics scan', 'impact check', 'who does this affect', 'is this safe to ship', any new feature proposal where stakeholder impact is unclear. Lightweight — takes minutes, not hours.

name: s4h-ethics-vendor-review
description: Evaluate a third-party vendor, supplier, partner, or integration against ethical standards before signing a contract or shipping their code or service. Use when considering a new supplier, SaaS tool, data provider, API integration, outsourcing arrangement, or partnership. TRIGGERS: 'vet this vendor', 'is this supplier ok', 'ethics check on this partner', 'should we use this third party', any third-party evaluation where labour practices, data handling, business model, or alignment with values is a consideration.

name: s4h-identity

name: s4h-investigation
description: Entry point for the investigation toolkit. Routes to the right investigation skill based on what you're trying to establish. Use when you say 'investigate', 'verify this', 'check this claim', 'where does this come from', 'is this true', 'trace the source', 'stress-test this belief', 'what's the evidence', 'could something else explain this', or want to know whether something you've heard is actually true.

name: s4h-investigation-claim-decomposition
description: Breaks a complex claim into its smallest independently verifiable parts, classifies each sub-claim, and identifies which parts carry the most logical load. Use when a claim feels too big to verify as a unit — 'what exactly is this claiming', 'break this down', 'what are the hidden assumptions in this statement', 'this seems like multiple claims at once', 'what would I need to verify to believe this'.

name: s4h-investigation-counter-hypothesis
description: Generates the best alternative explanations for the same observations. Use when you have a claim or explanation and want to know whether something else could explain the evidence just as well — 'could there be another explanation', 'what else could cause this', 'am I sure this isn't something else', 'steel-man the alternative', 'what would a skeptic say', 'rival hypotheses'.

name: s4h-investigation-evidence-audit

Covers evidence type hierarchy, sample quality, methodological soundness, conflicts of interest, and what's notably absent. Use when you want to know how good the evidence is — 'is this evidence strong', 'evaluate the research', 'how solid is this', 'is this just one study', 'what kind of evidence supports this', 'what's missing from the evidence'.

name: s4h-investigation-source-trace

name: s4h-linguistics-pragmatics

Use when you say 'what does this really mean', 'what is this message actually doing', 'is this a threat', 'what is being implied here', 'what does this leave unsaid', 'why does this feel off even though it seems polite', or when a communication seems fine on the surface but something is wrong underneath.
